criteria.name: voice_distinctness
criteria.description: No two characters need distinct voices, but the whole cast must not collapse into one. Test: if every character speaks in the same register — same sentence length, vocabulary, emotional temperature, so the scene reads as one voice with different names — score 0–35. If characters who should differ (a terse teen vs. a careful parent) audibly do, score 75+. Do not penalize two characters who legitimately share a voice (siblings, same upbringing).

criteria.name: scene_economy
criteria.description: Every line does dramatic work — advances tension, reveals character, or moves the situation forward. No filler exchanges ('Oh, I see.' / 'Yes, exactly.'). 8–14 lines total means each one must carry weight. Test: if lines could be cut without changing what the player knows or feels after the scene, score 0–40. If removing any line would lose something, score 70+.

criteria.name: naturalism
criteria.description: Read each spoken line aloud — would a real person say it that way in conversation? Lines must be plain spoken language by default. Three failure modes drag a scene into the uncanny: (a) figurative overshoot — a metaphor or simile where a person would speak plainly ('I'll let my pencil ride the wind like a kite across a blank page'); (b) a recurring image the same character keeps reaching for, so their speech reads as themed rather than spoken ('our bond is a ticket that never expires', 'keep our family's ticket from tearing in half'); (c) abstract interiority spoken aloud — narrating an inner state or idea instead of talking ('The carousel is just a space for what I see inside', 'The park's noise feels louder when they're apart'). Test: if a scene shows any of these more than once, score 0–40. If every line passes the say-it-aloud test and figurative language appears at most once, only on an emotionally charged line, score 75+.

criteria.name: subtext
criteria.description: Characters don't announce their emotional state or intentions directly. Meaning is conveyed through what they choose to say, avoid, or deflect. Test: if characters say 'I feel betrayed' or 'I want you to trust me,' score 0–40. If emotional states are legible through behavior and word choice without being stated, score 70+.

criteria.name: beat_fidelity
criteria.description: The script delivers what the beat summary promised — the specific confrontation, revelation, or decision described in beat_map. The location and characters present match. The script ends correctly per the node type (choice menu for branches, jump for linear nodes).
